content.title: About
content.content: Chiles rellenos is a classic Mexican dish consisting of large, mild peppers (often poblano) that are stuffed with cheese (sometimes combined with meat or vegetables) and then baked or fried. The cheese melts inside, giving the dish a creamy, rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: "Rellenos" comes from the Spanish verb "rellenar" meaning “to fill.”
Traditional recipes use poblano peppers, but other sweet peppers can be used.
The dish originated in the colonial era after the Spanish introduced cheese to Mexico.
Fillings vary widely—from simple mozzarella to blends of cheese, ham, rice, and spices.
Chiles rellenos are often served with a tomato‑chili sauce or a simple salsa.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein
items.content: When meat or beans are added, the dish becomes a good source of complete protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese and meat supply B2, B12, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Vitamin C from the pepper
items.content: Sweet peppers are rich in vitamin C, which boosts immunity and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Peppers contain carotenoids and other phytochemicals with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dairy products.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many cheeses are salty; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt varieties.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish can be high in calories due to cheese and cooking oil.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Remove seeds from the peppers, stuff them with grated cheese (optionally mixed with meat, rice or veggies), then bake at 180 °C for 20‑25 minutes or pan‑fry until golden. Serve hot, drizzled with tomato sauce, alongside rice, beans, or a fresh salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chiles rellenos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. They can also be frozen in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
